FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 24 April 1989, after the 
draft finalized by the Forestry and Plantation Machinery Sectional Committee had been approved 
by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 

Coagulation trays are used for the coagulation of natural rubber field latex for making sheet 
rubber. 

The shape of the tray specified in this standard helps in easy removal of the coagulum from it and 
also facilitates stacking of large number of trays together, one inside another within the minimum 
possible area. 

This standard has been prepared at the instance of the Rubber Board which has also provided 
the assistance in its preparation. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied 
with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be 
rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that 
of the specified value in this standard. 



IS 12653 : 1989 



Indian Standard 



RUBBER TAPPING TOOLS — COAGULATION 
TRAY — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifies material, dimensions, 
and other requirements of coagulation trays 
used for coagulation of natural rubber field 
latex. 

2 REFERENCES 

2.1 The following Indian Standards are neces- 
sary adjuncts to this standard: 



IS No. 



Title 



IS 21 : 1975 Specification * for wrought 
aluminium and aluminium 
alloys for manufacture ^of 
utensils ( third revision ) 

IS 9040 : 1978 Methods for sampling of utensils 

3 MATERIAL 

3.1 The trays shall be manufactured from 
aluminium alloy of Grade 19 000 or 31 000 of 
IS 21 : 1975. 

3.2 The thickness of sheet used shall be 1*25 mm, 
Min. 

4 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 

4.1 Typical shape of coagulation trays is shown 
in Fig. 1. The trays shall be so made as to rest 
in one another so that these may be stacked in 
a limited space. 

4.2 The dimensions of the coagulation trays 
shall be as given in Fig. 1. The dimensions shall 
have the following tolerances:

4.3 The reduction in thickness of coagulation 
trays after drawing shall not exceed 0*30 mm. 



All dimensions in millimetres. 

Fig. 1 Coagulation Trays 

5 CAPACITY 

5.1 The capacity of the coagulation tray 
for the dimensions given in Fig. 1 shall be 
8*0 ± 0*3 litres. 

6 MASS 

6.1 The mass of the coagulation tray for the 
dimensions given in Fig. 1 shall be 525 ± 25 g. 

7 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

7.1 Coagulation trays shall be pressed in one 
piece. Their corners shall be suitably reduced. 
The top edges of the trays and the bottoms shall 
be in one plane. The edges of the trays shall 
be rounded or suitably bent over to the under- 
side. When bent over, they shall be pressed as 
not to leave any crevice. 

7.2 The trays shall be finished bright all over. 
The pressing of the trays shall be such that they 
shall be cleanable thoroughly by ordinary 
method of cleaning by hand, brush or scrub. 
The trays shall be free from distortion, dents, 
wrinkles, scratches, pittings, deep tool marks, 
and other surface defects. 



1 



IS 12553 : 1989 



8 MARKING 



8.1 Each tray shall be suitably marked at the 
bottom with the manufacturer's name, trade- 
mark or identification mark and the correspond- 
ing grade of aluminium. The impression of 
the marking shall not show up on the inside of 
the tray. 



9 PACKING 

9.1 Trays shall be packed in accordance with the 
best trade practices. Care shall be taken to see 
that the trays do not get dented during transit. 

10 SAMPLING 

10.1 The sampling of the trays shall be done in 
accordance with IS 9040 : 1978. 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards 
Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products 
covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with 
the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality 
control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked 
products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safe- 
guard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted 
to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification 
of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in 
the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or 
grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), 
BIS.
